title: Joined the 2026 Epic AI MegaJam and spent almost 40 hours over the weekend wrestling with Astra
author: Bright-Management-27
selftext:
I’ve been making a few games with AI as an after-work hobby, and I wanted to see how far I could get in a limited amount of time, so I decided to join this jam. Is it just me, or does Astra seem to understand prompts worse lately than when it first came out?  


**Play here:** [https://studio-rhei.itch.io/shoguns-castle](https://studio-rhei.itch.io/shoguns-castle)

comments.author: Crazy_Ad_3147
comments.body:
Look well done awesome effort but we have to ban ai vibe coding for game jams.. like you wouldnt have the slightest clue about how to actually build any of it, and game jams "were" filled people who CAN, and they want to network, they dont want to network with vibe coders who really have clue about the code.

Just an fyi hey - not having a go at you, I just read this all the time - so i do this in my down time, spare time, hobby and its fine, but dont tell me you are a coder/game dev.  

I am a 30 plus year software dev and look I do use AI as it speeds up my workflow, but it makes people think they are at my level when you are not.

Thats what people are upset about, they cant built this is 40hours by themselves but you'll come along and say its easy and a high level whilst not knowing any code.

but good effort you know how to use a computer really :)

replies.author: Bright-Management-27
replies.body: Thanks for checking it out! Just to clarify, this was the Epic AI MegaJam, a jam specifically built around using AI tools, so AI use was the whole point here. I also never said it was easy. It honestly took a lot of wrestling to get it working. For what it’s worth, I’ve been a developer for 26 years, and I worked in the game industry until about 8 years ago. Fair point on the broader debate about regular jams, though.
